Categories with low vehicle counts or short time durations of driving are shaded pale orange; previously, we shaded using yellow, but that conflicts with the yellow line colors for late hours of the day. For each hour line shown, the fractions sum to 1 across all speed bins. We output the average speed distributions to the file SpeedDistributionResults_byHour_source_fdna.csv and SpeedDistributionResults__byHour_vocation_fdna.csv for source types and vocations, respectively. Figure 18 shows the speed bin distribution based on the FleetDNA combination-unit long-haul vehicle source type. This category had some of the most vehicles and recorded hours in the data density section, and that has led to smooth rather than sporadic hour lines; for example, we will see future graphs where 100% of the time is spent in a single speed bin due to very few recorded seconds at the midnight hour, but we do not see any of that behavior in this chart. Interestingly, long-haul trucks have very consistent behavior at different hours of the day. For rural roads and urban freeways, these trucks spend most of their time at 65 mph regardless of hour of the day. An exception is for rural other roads on weekdays—we see a purple line from the early morning hours that has a higher percent time spent at under 10 mph. Also, urban freeways on weekends have some variability in the midnight hours, with more percent time spent at 60, 70, or 80 mph for different hour IDs. Long-haul trucks on urban other roads have a different speed bin distribution from the rest, with a more even spread of speeds between 5 and 65 mph and peaks at 5 mph. This unique behavior could be due to speed limits or congestion on these roads. It is interesting that the main peak for rural other roads appears at 65 mph like freeways, but we suspect this high-speed behavior is because TomTom road type 1 was mapped to “other roads” even though it includes highways used for national travel, just not designated as an official motorway (TomTom 2022). On other roads on weekends, some late-night hours have less data. We recommend replacing rural other road hours 21–24 with the speed distribution from hour ID 20, as well as replacing hour ID 1 with the distribution from hour ID 2 and inputting the distribution from hour ID 4 into hour ID 3.
